# Does the record already survive to trace time?

**Generated from `docs/store_time_role_durability.json`. Do not edit this file.** Rebuild
with `python -m benchmarks.store_time_role_durability --measure`; `--check` validates.

## What was asked

Whether the engine must record the licensing role pair on each schema-primed prediction so
Q028's trace can name it. The engine already writes the pair on two rows -- the schema
carries `source_role_id` and `target_role_id`, the prediction carries `schema_prior` -- so
the question is whether those rows are still there when the trace reads them.

## What was run

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| World | the campaign's two context worlds, `VOCAB_A` then `VOCAB_B` |
| Seed | `20261101` (the trace's calibration seed, outside CCRE-2's confirmatory block) |
| Cycles | 40 + 40 |
| Stored sleep rows read | 16962 |
| Role rows among them | 302 |
| Scan window | 200000 events, truncated: False |
| Decision rule, fixed before the run | all primed predictions recoverable from stored rows -> NO_ENGINE_CHANGE; any missing leg -> ENGINE_CHANGE_NEEDED, with the leg named; no primed prediction -> NOT_MEASURABLE |

## Controls, run before the measurement

| control | expected | observed | passed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `empty_denominator_is_not_measurable` | `measurable=False` | `measurable=False` | yes |
| `ids_stripped` | `R3_schema_without_role_ids` | `R3_schema_without_role_ids` | yes |
| `recoverable` | `recoverable` | `recoverable` | yes |
| `role_absent` | `R2_role_rows_absent` | `R2_role_rows_absent` | yes |
| `schema_absent` | `R1_schema_absent` | `R1_schema_absent` | yes |

A classifier that answers `recoverable` for everything was rejected: yes.

## What survived

| `R1_schema_absent` | 0 |
| `R2_role_rows_absent` | 0 |
| `R3_schema_without_role_ids` | 0 |

| quantity | value |
| --- | --- |
| primed predictions (denominator) | 405 |
| recoverable from stored rows | 405 |
| share | 1.0000 |
| decision | **NO_ENGINE_CHANGE** |

## The decision

**No engine change.** Every primed prediction's role pair is recoverable from the rows the engine already writes, on the cell the trace will read. A `schema_prior_roles` field would be a second copy of `schema_prior` plus the schema row, and Q028's trace does not need it; the pair resolver is the whole fix.

## What this does not establish

- **One cell, one seed.** It is the cell the trace will read, not a distribution; pruning
  that needs more than 80 cycles is not exercised.
- **Survival is not resolution.** A recoverable pair still needs the pair resolver to read
  it; this measures whether the record is present, not whether Q028 is answered.
- **The window was widened deliberately.** The engine's own loader reads a bounded recency
  window, so this reads every stored sleep row; a missing row here is missing from the
  record, not from the reader.
